The bundled Q(sqrt(2)) checker verifies the finite geometry and p=2 endpoint; no continuum claim is inferred from sampling.

value.rationale: This closes the natural modified counterpart of a canonical 2017 regular-octagon exponent computation exactly where the unrestricted and equal-radius normalizations differ. The result gives a complete sub-Hilbert profile and an exact phase boundary at p=2, which is directly relevant to interpreting the modified constant used in later Hilbert/uniform-nonsquareness characterizations. It is a natural classification and comparison, not an arbitrary finite slice or a numerical recomputation.
